title: Information Imbalance and Imbalance Gain
text: Imbalance Gain (IG) quantifies information imbalance variable \(X\) provides future state another variable \(Y\). assess information transfer \(X \rightarrow Y\), IG compares neighborhood structure future state \(Y\) augmented present state containing \(X\) \(Y\). basic quantity Information Imbalance two distance spaces \(\) \(B\): \[ \Delta(\rightarrow B) = \frac{2}{N} \left\langle r^B \mid r^\leq k \right\rangle, \] \(r^\) \(r^B\) distance ranks spaces \(\) \(B\), respectively, \(k\) number nearest neighbors considered. small \(\Delta(\rightarrow B)\) indicates points close \(\) also tend close \(B\). distance rank one space therefore provides information structure another space. \(X \rightarrow Y\), let \(d_Y(0)\) denote distance space constructed present state \(Y\), let \(d_{XY}^{\alpha}(0)\) denote corresponding space incorporating \(X\) relative scaling parameter \(\alpha\). future state \(Y\) represented \(d_Y(\tau)\), \(\tau\) prediction horizon. Imbalance Gain evaluates \[ \Delta(\alpha) = \Delta \left(d_{XY}^{\alpha}(0) \rightarrow d_Y(\tau) \right). \] \(X\) contains information future \(Y\), adding \(X\) reduce Information Imbalance. resulting Imbalance Gain \[ \delta\Delta(X \rightarrow Y) = 1 - \frac{\min_{\alpha}\Delta(\alpha)}{\Delta(0)}. \] , \(\Delta(0)\) represents prediction using \(Y\) alone, whereas \(\min_{\alpha}\Delta(\alpha)\) represents best prediction obtained incorporating information \(X\). \(\delta\Delta(X \rightarrow Y)=0\) indicates gain adding \(X\), positive value indicates \(X\) provides additional information future state \(Y\). calculation can performed opposite direction, \(Y\rightarrow X\), allowing directional information transfer assessed directions.

title: Information Imbalance and Imbalance Gain
text: Conditional Imbalance Gain (CIG) extends Imbalance Gain assess additional information provided \(X\) future state \(Y\) conditional third variable \(Z\). present state \(Z\) incorporated baseline prediction, contribution \(X\) evaluated relative baseline. Let \(d_{YZ}^{\alpha_Z}(0)\) denote distance space constructed present states \(Y\) \(Z\), \(\alpha_Z\) controlling relative scaling \(Z\). incorporating \(X\) scaling parameter \(\alpha_X\), augmented distance space denoted \(d_{XYZ}^{\alpha_X,\alpha_Z}(0)\). Conditional Imbalance Gain defined \[ \delta \Delta (X \rightarrow Y \mid Z) = 1- \frac{ \min\limits_{\alpha_X,\alpha_Z} \Delta \left( d_{XYZ}^{\alpha_X,\alpha_Z}(0) \rightarrow d_Y(\tau) \right)} {\min\limits_{\alpha_Z} \Delta \left(d_{YZ}^{\alpha_Z}(0) \rightarrow d_Y(\tau) \right)}. \] denominator represents best prediction future state \(Y\) using \(Y\) \(Z\) present state. numerator represents best prediction additionally incorporating \(X\). positive \(\delta\Delta(X\rightarrow Y\mid Z)\) indicates \(X\) provides additional predictive information future state \(Y\) beyond contained \(Y\) \(Z\). fixed \(\alpha_X\), corresponding conditional Imbalance Gain \[ \delta \Delta(X\rightarrow Y\mid Z;\alpha_X) = 1- \frac{ \min\limits_{\alpha_Z} \Delta \left(d_{XYZ}^{\alpha_X,\alpha_Z}(0)  \rightarrow d_Y(\tau) \right)} {\min\limits_{\alpha_Z} \Delta \left( d_{YZ}^{\alpha_Z}(0) \rightarrow d_Y(\tau) \right)}. \] optimal \(\alpha_X\) can obtained minimizing conditional Information Imbalance range \(\alpha_X\). formulation can applied reverse direction assess \(Y\rightarrow X\mid Z\).

title: Synergistic-Unique-Redundant Decomposition of Causality
text: Understanding causal influences combine interact essential complex systems. Synergistic–Unique–Redundant Decomposition (SURD) method provides principled way break total information flow variables : Unique contributions — information uniquely provided one driver; Redundant contributions — information shared multiple drivers; Synergistic contributions — information revealed drivers considered together.

title: Synergistic-Unique-Redundant Decomposition of Causality
text: vignette utilizes classic neural tube defects (NTD) dataset, widely used geographical detector tutorials demonstrate use SURD. First, install required R packages run subsequent code: , load preprocess NTD dataset gdverse package: NTD dataset can visualized follows: continuous response variable (NTD incidence rate), systematically evaluated five discretization methods (standard deviation, equal interval, quantile, natural breaks, head/tail breaks) combined class numbers ranging 3 10. specific discretization scheme maximized unique information SURD results selected process NTD incidence rate final analysis. particularly important note surd_discrete function infoxtr can handle entirely discrete data; continuous inputs can discretized using appropriate methods prior use. optimal parameter combination among candidates discretize NTD incidence three classes using natural breaks method. run code obtain final results: simplify visualization, plotting function provided , produces SURD decomposition plot — grouped bar chart unique (U), synergistic (S), redundant (R) components, along side panel showing information leak. SURD results shown figure : can also generate result plot actual variable names, visualized : 🧩 See also: ?infoxtr::surd() function details. spEDM package spatial empirical dynamic modeling. tEDM package temporal empirical dynamic modeling. pc package pattern causality analysis.

title: Knockoff Conditional Mutual Information — kocmi
text: data Observation data. target Integer vector column indices target variables. agent Integer vector column indices agent variables. conds Integer vector column indices conditioning variables. knockoff Knockoff realizations constructed agent variable keeping target variable unchanged. column corresponds one Monte Carlo knockoff sample generated using remaining variables except target. null_knockoff (optional) Knockoff realizations generated null setting variables jointly used construct knockoffs. column represents one Monte Carlo sample. contain_null = FALSE, argument can NULL. type (optional) Estimation method: "disc" discrete mutual information "cont" continuous mutual information (KSG estimator). nboots (optional) Number permutations used sign-flipping permutation test evaluating significance mean information difference. k (optional) type = "cont", number nearest neighbors used continuous conditional mutual information estimator. type = "disc", number bins used discretization. threads (optional) Number threads used. seed (optional) Random seed used permutation test. base (optional) Logarithm base entropy. Defaults exp(1) (nats). Use 2 bits 10 dits. method (optional) Discretization method. One "sd", "equal", "geometric", "quantile", "natural("jenks")", "headtail"("headtails"). contain_null (optional) Logical. TRUE, test statistic computed using knockoffs generated null model (provided null_knockoff). case difference defined \((Y; X_{null} | Z) - (Y; X_{knockoff} | Z)\). FALSE, original conditional mutual information \((Y; X | Z)\) used instead compared knockoff estimates \((Y; X_{knockoff} | Z)\).
